descriptions.gradient: Smooth linear ramp. Base for skies, fades, and masks.
descriptions.noise: Fractal noise. General-purpose surface variation and grunge.
descriptions.cloud: Soft billowing noise. Skies, smoke, vapour.
descriptions.voronoi: Cellular chunks. Stone, cracked plates, organic cells.
descriptions.veins: Voronoi distance-to-edge. Cracks, leaf veins, dry riverbeds.
descriptions.scales: Offset cellular grid. Reptile scales, fish, armour plating.
descriptions.stripes: Hard or soft banding. Fabric, warning markings, ribbing.
descriptions.wood: Distorted rings. Timber grain, tree cross-sections.
descriptions.marble: Turbulent banding. Marble, swirled stone, oil-on-water.
descriptions.weave: Crossed waves. Woven cloth, baskets, mesh.
descriptions.plasma: Layered noise into a wide colour sweep. Energy, magic, heat.
descriptions.fire: Vertically-masked noise into a heat ramp. Flame, lava, embers.
descriptions.sparks: Sparse bright points. Embers, glints, star fields.

response.result:
Texture wood_floor imported as material. Created material 'wood_floor' with maps: Diffuse, Rough, Displacement, nor_gl. Nothing is using it yet - call set_texture to apply it to an object. Saving the file before then discards it, as Blender does with any unused datablock, and it would have to be downloaded again. The texture covers 1.7m x 1.7m in the real world. Its 'Mapping' node is in POINT mode, where Scale multiplies the UV coordinates: the pattern repeats Scale times across whatever span the UVs cover. For UVs that run 0-1 across a surface, life-sized tiling is Scale = surface size in metres / 1.7.

From Poly Haven by Dimitrios Savva - https://polyhaven.com/a/wood_floor (CC0, free to use for anything).
